surfaces.part: fur cone body with door opening

answer.evidence: The silhouette widens by a steady 2 px every 2 rows, from 10 px at row 7 to 45 px at row 46, which is a flat triangle seen face-on. The fur body (rows 9-40) is a continuous vertical face with a dark door opening at rows 28-40. There is no horizontal band, no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse anywhere. The apex (rows 7-13) is only a narrow tie and the poles above it are thin diagonal lines. The base at rows 40-46 is a snow and dirt strip along the ground, not a top surface. The tent shows no top, so it reads as a front elevation, not a three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts match the references: 12 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10, 2% near-flat coverage, and 9% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines lean brown rather than black. By eye, the fur body has only about 4 steps (light tan, mid brown, dark brown, deep shadow) with a few hide streaks, while the Beodeul roofs carry 5-6 steps with per-tile highlights and scallops. The candidate is also tiny and has a simple conical form with a small snow base, so it is sparse next to the full houses. It reads as a clean piece with tinted outlines and no big flat fills, but it is thinner and less textured than the references, with little grain on the hide surface. Sparse and small is acceptable, yet a careful artist would see it as slightly flatter than the references, so it falls short.
